title: Velcro's First Version Didn't Work
title_options: Velcro Started With Hooks Grabbing Hooks
sources_on_screen: RTS, 10 Jul 1961 and 15 Dec 1984 (de Mestral interviews)
US Air Force AMRL report, Jan 1963

beats.say: Velcro's first design had no loops at all. Just hooks, grabbing other hooks.
beats.vis: Two strips bristling with hooks pressed together; most slide past each other.

beats.say: Its inventor, George de Mestral, later said it began in nineteen forty-one, coming home from a hunting trip.
beats.vis: Jura scenery as in the 1961 film: spruce forest, meadow, dry-stone wall. No Alps. George in a felt hat with a shotgun (1984 look, C052).

beats.say: Burrs had gripped his trousers, and his dog's ears.
beats.vis: Burrs on trouser legs and on a dog's floppy ears. Breed ARTISTIC (C024).

beats.say: Under a microscope, he said, the hooks looked like tiny chamois horns. A perfection.
beats.vis: Dive into the burr; hook tips curl like small horns.

beats.say: Then, he said, the idea slept for about ten years. Until one day he thought: if I can make hooks like these, I'll have made a fastener.
beats.vis: The burr goes into a drawer; pages flip; the drawer opens again.

beats.say: In nineteen fifty-one he applied for a patent. Loop a nylon thread over a hot bar, so it keeps its shape. Then snip one side, and the loop becomes a hook.
beats.vis: Patent Fig. 1 animated: loop over a glowing bar, knife cuts one side, hook springs up.

beats.say: And luck helped. He said a storeroom worker sent the wrong thread by mistake, and the thread they had ordered would never have worked.
beats.vis: Storeroom shelf; a hand takes the wrong spool; a red X on the ordered spool, a glowing tick on the wrong one.

beats.say: But his first design pressed hooks against hooks. His own later patent says only about thirty percent of them caught.
beats.vis: Grid of hooks: 3 in 10 light up. '~30%'.

beats.say: So in nineteen fifty-seven, he turned one side into soft loops. About a thousand in every square centimetre, so far more hooks find something to grab.
beats.vis: The bottom strip becomes a dense loop field; nearly all hooks light up. '1 cm²: ~1,000 loops'.

beats.say: And a 2015 study found that Velcro's hooks work less like a burr's than like a different plant's.
beats.vis: Needle-like burr hook beside a Velcro hook; a question mark becomes a small woodland plant (name off screen).

beats.say: By nineteen sixty-three, the US Air Force had stuck it to an aircraft's ceiling, so people in loop-soled gym shoes could try to walk on it, weightless. Later, it flew on Apollo.
beats.vis: Cut-away plane; a person upside down on a hook-lined ceiling track; then a capsule interior.
beats.src_line: US Air Force AMRL, Jan 1963 · NASA

beats.say: He called the invention five percent of the work. The rest was sweat. Would you have kept going?
beats.vis: Back to the two hook strips; they peel apart; the desk drawer closes.

voice_note: Name pronunciation pending AK's ear check (C053): the 1961/1984 narrators seem to drop the s ('de Métral').
